stories.headline: Long-context inference gets 30x faster by skipping most attention calculations
stories.summary: Processing a 128,000-token context through a language model is expensive because every token attends to every other. FlashPrefill V2, an arXiv preprint, skips most of those calculations using block-sparse patterns, achieving a 30x speedup over a dense baseline on NVIDIA H20 hardware. It integrates with SGLang today. Benchmark against your longest production contexts before committing.
stories.take: Long-context serving costs were set by dense attention; sparse block selection now cuts that by 30x.

stories.headline: NVIDIA's agent architecture scores perfectly on a hard general-reasoning benchmark
stories.summary: NVIDIA's Agentic Variation Operators (AVO) scored perfectly on ARC-AGI-3, a benchmark where agents must explore unknown environments without instructions or goals. The same architecture ran a seven-day GPU-kernel optimisation loop, outperforming established libraries by up to 10.5%. When does your long-horizon agent task share enough structure with this benchmark to treat the result as a reliable baseline?
stories.take: Agent harness design now sets the benchmark ceiling, where model choice set it before.

stories.headline: NVIDIA maps where security must live in an agent stack
stories.summary: NVIDIA's security team draws a line most stacks blur: harnesses guide what an agent tries; infrastructure determines what it can do. Three named gaps — unclear boundaries, excessive credentials, untrusted data as control — let agents exceed scope. Does your runtime enforce policy before the harness loads, or can the agent simply decline the control?
stories.take: Infrastructure enforcement now sets the agent's authority ceiling; harness logic set it before.

claims.note: The take accurately captures the source's argument that infrastructure is the authoritative control layer, with the harness being a behavioral (non-authoritative) guide.

stories.headline: LinkedIn's production code review runs multiple competing AI agents to cut noise
stories.summary: LinkedIn replaced a single AI reviewer with multiple independent agents on distinct models; convergence across agents signals high confidence, divergence triggers separate verification. Across 5,230 sampled comments, 63.9% of suggestions were accepted by developers. When you're choosing a code review architecture, is one model's blind spots acceptable at your PR volume?
stories.take: Engineering leads at scale now own an agent-orchestration problem, not a model-selection one.

stories.headline: Retrieved memories can trap language models into wrong reasoning
stories.summary: An arXiv preprint introduces MemTrapBench, a benchmark covering two failure modes where retrieved memories hurt rather than help: Reasoning Fixation and Belief Distortion. Across five memory frameworks, every tested strategy underperformed the no-memory baseline, with the strongest dropping more than 10%. Run MemTrapBench against your memory stack; if you score below baseline, AdaptiveMem is the named mitigation.
stories.take: Correct retrieval was the assumed ceiling for memory quality; it is now the floor of a harder problem.

stories.headline: Google open-sources a compiler that runs AI models on encrypted data
stories.summary: Google's HEIR compiler adapts existing PyTorch models to run on homomorphic-encrypted inputs, so the server never sees raw data. The toolchain is open-source with demos included. Overhead is real: addition costs ~100ms per operation, and Google ships benchmarking code but no language-model figures. Pull the repo and run HEIR against your smallest production classifier before committing to the architecture.
stories.take: Encrypted-data inference shifts from research curiosity to a compiler you can clone today.

stories.summary: Full Chromium browsers were built for humans; Cloudflare's Kitesurf runs browser components in isolated WebAssembly/Rust environments on Workers, supporting Playwright and Puppeteer with lower resource overhead. Each page gets its own sandboxed worker. Cloudflare says open-sourcing is planned; wire Playwright against Kitesurf in your next browser-use agent build once it lands.

stories.headline: Ora's live benchmarks show 99% of websites block AI agents mid-task
stories.summary: Ora spawns agents against live customer sites with instructions to sign up, integrate, and pay. By Ora's own measure, 99% of the web isn't agent-ready. Testing covers Claude Code, ChatGPT, Gemini, and others; one benchmark run surfaced a caching fix that cut total costs roughly 15%. Run your own site through journey.ora.ai before your next agent deployment.
stories.take: Product teams shipping agentic workflows now inherit a web-readiness audit, not just a model choice.
